note: The alate part is based on dealated females (morphotype and paramorphotypes, n=2), and the antennae are broken in the specimens, so the number of segments is unknown; the soldier is based on the holotype and three series of paratypes. The material from the Congo recorded by Kirby between 1942—1945 as 'Glyptotermes sp. nov.' is this species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text:
The dealated adult is close to G. longuisculus, from which it differs in the narrower head, the less swollen and differently shaped eyes, the slightly circular ocelli, the narrower pronotum with narrower anterolateral corners and more nearly straight sides, the slightly concave posterior margin, the slightly smaller wing scales and the shorter tibiae. Compared with G. ignotus, G. reticulatus and Glyptotermes sinomalatus all parts of this species are larger; compared with G. kawandae the head and pronotum are smaller and the ocelli touch the eyes; compared with G. insulanus it is smaller overall and the eyes are of a different shape. The soldier is close to that of G. longuisculus, from which it differs in the shallower median depression of the frons, the anterior dorsal margin of the frons not raised into lateral projections and the longer anterior third of the postmentum; compared with G. hendrickxi the head is shorter, narrower and thinner, the projection of the frontal face less prominent and the pronotum shorter and narrower.

The type locality is Kakitumba, Rwanda-Urundi (1°04′ S, 30°26′ E); the holotype soldier and paratypes were collected by H. Kirby on 28 December 1934 (month 12), number T-3022; paratypes were also collected in Kivu, Congo, below the Mulungu road and 5 km north-west of the crossroads south of Beni (altitude 3600 feet, edge of rainforest). The species is named after Dr Thomas Park, professor of zoology at the University of Chicago.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Dealated female. Head and pronotum rusty brown; labrum, antennae and legs brownish yellow; nota rusty brown, paler than the head and pronotum; wing scales smoky brown. Head with a few sparse short erect setae; margins and disc of the pronotum with both long and short setae. Head evenly rounded behind the eyes. Y-suture present but indistinct because the head colour is dark. Eyes small, not much swollen, shaped as figured. Ocelli oval, touching the eyes. Antennae broken off; segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, segment 4 shorter than segment 3. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior margin broadly and evenly concave, anterolateral corners narrow, sides sometimes straight, posterior margin straight.

Measurements of 2 female dealated adults (range / mean): head length (to the tip of the labrum) 1.13 mm; head length (to the base of the mandibles) 0.90—0.94 mm / 0.92 mm; head width 0.94 mm; eye diameter 0.29 mm; distance from the lower margin of the eye 0.13—0.14 mm / 0.14 mm; ocellus length 0.08 mm; pronotum median length 0.53—0.60 mm / 0.56 mm; pronotum maximum length 0.60—0.68 mm / 0.64 mm; pronotum width 0.79—0.86 mm / 0.82 mm; length of the hind tibia 0.79 mm; forewing scale length 0.75 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head brownish yellow posteriorly and laterally, brown at the Y-suture and on both sides of the eyes, the frontal region reddish brown; mandibles dark reddish brown at the base, glossy and nearly black at the apex; labrum pale yellow; eyes nearly white; antennae yellow; pronotum brownish yellow; legs pale yellow; nota nearly white with a yellow tinge. Head with a few sparse short setae; margins and disc of the pronotum with a few long and numerous short setae; labrum with about 8—9 long setae. Head long, sides parallel, slightly constricted in front of the antennal sockets; middle of the frons broadly concave; anterodorsal projection faintly visible; frontal face forming a slope of about 45° in lateral view. Y-suture clearly visible. Eyes small. Posterolateral margins of the labrum parallel, converging forwards into a blunt point. Mandibles short, the outer base irregular; left mandible with 3 marginal teeth; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, the tip of the first marginal tooth lying 0.30 mm from the tip of the apical tooth. Postmentum long, distinctly constricted in the proximal half, the sides converging forwards from the widest point, anterior margin almost straight. Antennae 11—13-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segment 2 longer than or equal to segment 4. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, anterior margin broadly angular, anterolateral corners narrow; posterolateral margins broadly rounded in specimens from the type nest and less bluntly rounded in paratype-nest specimens; posterior margin slightly concave in the middle. Femora not inflated.

Soldier measurements (holotype; range of paratypes): head length (to the base of the mandibles) 1.73 mm / 1.65—1.84 mm; head width 1.13 mm / 0.99—1.11 mm; head height 1.05 mm / 0.92—1.05 mm; length of the left mandible 0.83 mm / 0.75—0.84 mm; postmentum maximum width 0.45 mm / 0.41—0.45 mm; postmentum minimum width 0.23 mm / 0.13—0.23 mm; postmentum length 1.28 mm / 1.13—1.31 mm; pronotum median length 0.60 mm / 0.49—0.60 mm; pronotum maximum length 0.62 mm / 0.60—0.68 mm; pronotum width 1.01 mm / 0.90—1.09 mm; length of the hind tibia 0.75 mm / 0.68—0.75 mm.
